# SqlArtisan

> A type-safe SQL query builder for C# (.NET 8). You write SQL-like C# and it
> produces the SQL string plus its bind parameters. The SQL you write is the SQL
> that runs — cross-database portability is a deliberate non-goal. Supported
> dialects: MySQL, Oracle, PostgreSQL, SQLite, SQL Server (default: PostgreSQL).

Each reference page pairs the C# you write with the exact SQL it emits. When
generating code, pick the API for the target DBMS; do not expect a single call to
be rewritten across dialects.

## Docs

- [Overview & Quick Start](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/h-tacayama/SqlArtisan/main/README.md): Why SqlArtisan, key features, performance, packages, getting started (prerequisites, installation, quick start), configuration, design philosophy, and pointers to the docs, versioning, contributing, the changelog and the license.
- [Reference Home](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/h-tacayama/SqlArtisan/main/docs/README.md): Index of the guides, the query cookbook, and every statement, expression, function and analyzer section.

## Reference

- [Query Statements](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/h-tacayama/SqlArtisan/main/docs/query-statements.md): SELECT (clauses, JOIN, set operators, pagination, FOR UPDATE, PostgreSQL `FROM UNNEST`), INSERT (multi-row, SET-like, INSERT…SELECT, UPSERT, MERGE), UPDATE, DELETE (correlated and joined forms; correlated forms require an aliased target), WITH/CTE, RETURNING, OUTPUT (SQL Server).
- [Expressions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/h-tacayama/SqlArtisan/main/docs/expressions.md): NULL, arithmetic, `INTERVAL` date-shift expressions (MySQL's bound `Interval(...)`; the quoted `IntervalLiteral(...)` on MySQL, Oracle and PostgreSQL, in forms that differ by dialect), string concatenation (`||` vs `CONCAT`), conditions, JSON operators (`->`, `->>`, `#>`, `#>>`, JSONB `@>`/`?`/`?|`/`?&`), array operators (`ARRAY[...]`, `&&`, `@>`, `<@`), vector distance operators (`<->`, `<=>`, `<#>` on Oracle and PostgreSQL; `<+>`, `<~>`, `<%>` on PostgreSQL only; all six through the pgvector extension on PostgreSQL), full-text search (MySQL `MATCH ... AGAINST`, Oracle `CONTAINS`/`SCORE`, PostgreSQL `@@`/`TO_TSVECTOR`/`TO_TSQUERY`, SQLite FTS5 `MATCH`, SQL Server `CONTAINS`/`FREETEXT`), scalar subqueries, ALL/ANY/SOME (subquery and PostgreSQL `= ANY(:param)` array-bind forms), CASE, CAST, window functions, conditional aggregation, string aggregation, sequences.
- [Functions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/h-tacayama/SqlArtisan/main/docs/functions.md): Built-in function catalog — numeric, character, date/time, conversion, comparison, JSON (`JSON_EXTRACT`, `JSON_VALUE`, `JSON_QUERY`), full-text search, aggregate, string aggregation, window/analytic — plus bind-parameter types.
- [Analyzer](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/h-tacayama/SqlArtisan/main/docs/analyzer.md): Opt-in Roslyn analyzer that reports configuration problems; constructs, identifiers and argument values a configured target dialect (or any dialect in a configured set) doesn't support; what the generated table class's schema metadata says about the query; and validity problems — a correlated DML target `Build()` would reject, or C# that binds a value instead of building SQL. Sections: enabling it, the rules (SQLA0001–SQLA0302), checking a set of dialects at once, migrating from the legacy target key, override keys, version-aware warnings, context rules, argument value validity, the correlated DML target, C# fallbacks, schema-aware warnings, mixed-dialect projects, CI gates, verified-against versions, known limitations.
- [Query Cookbook](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/h-tacayama/SqlArtisan/main/docs/cookbook.md): Realistic end-to-end queries with the exact emitted SQL, pinned by unit tests — everyday patterns (a paginated list with a reusable query, a filtered aggregate report, a custom CASE sort), reporting (top-N per group, pivoting rows to columns, rows without a match), dynamic search screens (optional filters, runtime sort, shared COUNT), batch/UPSERT/MERGE DML.

## Guides

- [Comparison Guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/h-tacayama/SqlArtisan/main/docs/comparison.md): How SqlArtisan compares to EF Core, linq2db, SqlKata, Dapper.SqlBuilder, and InterpolatedSql — philosophy, type safety, machine-verifiability, dialect handling, execution, performance, and when NOT to choose SqlArtisan.
- [Dapper + SqlArtisan from Scratch](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/h-tacayama/SqlArtisan/main/docs/guides/dapper-quickstart.md): The greenfield path — packages, table classes (generated or hand-written), executing queries through `SqlArtisan.Dapper`, pointers to the reference for writing statements, pinning queries with tests.
- [Oracle Array-Bind Execution with SqlArtisan.ArrayBind](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/h-tacayama/SqlArtisan/main/docs/guides/oracle-array-bind.md): Run SqlArtisan-built statements for N rows in one round trip via ODP.NET array binding — installing the package, building one statement per row, executing them in a transaction, UPDATE and DELETE beyond INSERT, and the loud-failure guards.
- [Using SqlArtisan with AI Coding Assistants](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/h-tacayama/SqlArtisan/main/docs/guides/ai-assistants.md): Feeding the assistant the reference, analyzer target configuration, keeping the table classes in step with the database, exact-SQL test pinning, and an agent-rules snippet for generated queries.

## Optional

- [Versioning & Support](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/h-tacayama/SqlArtisan/main/docs/versioning.md): SemVer commitment, what the public API is, breaking-change definition (including emitted-SQL changes, new rejections, the analyzer's diagnostic IDs and configuration, and TableClassGen's command-line surface), deprecation process, verified engine versions, support window, release cadence.
- [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/h-tacayama/SqlArtisan/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md): Version history — a browse link, not a raw one, so the accumulated change log (which names since-removed APIs) stays out of the `llms-full.txt` deep bundle, like the ADRs.
- [Design (ADRs)](https://github.com/h-tacayama/SqlArtisan/tree/main/docs/adr): Architecture decisions — SQL fidelity and dialect handling, automatic parameterization, public API shape, performance, the analyzer's design, the validity-enforcement boundary for AI-assisted SQL, which text positions are bound, escaped, or emitted verbatim, and how precisely the docs may state engine behavior.
